draft.title: The Provisional Government and the Soviets
card: After Nicholas II gave up the throne in March 1917 (new style), a Provisional Government took over. It was formed by members of the old Duma, and its leaders were mostly liberals and moderates. It was meant to rule until an elected assembly could decide Russia's future.
it held official authority and ran the ministries, but it had not been elected and had little means of enforcing its orders.
a council of elected delegates from workers and soldiers. It did not rule formally, but workers and soldiers in the capital listened to it.

The Soviet's Order No. 1 told soldiers to obey the Provisional Government only when the Soviet agreed. This split is called dual power: the government had the legal right to rule, and the Soviet had much of the real support. The two often clashed, so the arrangement was uneasy.
draft.remember: Dual power: the government held formal authority, but the Soviet held much of the real support.

a.q: Why is the situation in Russia in 1917 called dual power?
opts: Two bodies each held part of the power, and often clashed
Nicholas II and the Duma ruled the empire together
Two Soviets in different cities each ruled their own region
The government and the Soviet agreed on every policy
a.why: The Provisional Government had official authority, while the Petrograd Soviet had the support of workers and soldiers. Neither could fully control the other. The option about agreement is wrong because the two often clashed.
a.clue: Think about who had the legal right to rule and who had the support.

b.q: In 1917, a Provisional Government minister orders troops in Petrograd to move to the front. Why might the order fail?
opts: Soldiers were told to obey it only if the Soviet agreed
The government had been elected to rule only the Duma
The Soviet had formally replaced the government as ruler
All the soldiers had gone home when the tsar abdicated
b.why: Order No. 1 told soldiers to obey the government only when the Soviet agreed. So the government held formal authority but could not rely on its orders being followed. The Soviet had not formally replaced the government, which is why the power was shared.
b.clue: Recall what Order No. 1 told soldiers to do.

a.best: Two bodies each held part of the power, and often clashed

b.best: Soldiers were told to obey it only if the Soviet agreed
